circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: The Yas Marina Circuit is a 5. 281 km track located on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, designed by Hermann Tilke, which has been the venue for the Formula One season finale since 2009. It represents the second of four Middle Eastern Formula One circuits, following Bahrain and preceding those in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street track that encircles Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb and hosts the annual Formula One Australian Grand Prix alongside various supporting racing categories. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification for motorsport events.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326-kilometer circuit originally operated as the Österreichring and served as the venue for the Austrian Grand Prix throughout the 1970s and 1980s. Following renovation and redesign, the track was rebranded and returned to hosting the Austrian Grand Prix during the late 1990s and early 2000s.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street racing venue in Azerbaijan's capital that spans 6. 003 km, ranking as the fourth-longest track in Formula One competition. Following its debut as the venue for the 2016 European Grand Prix, the circuit established itself as a permanent fixture on the championship calendar in 2017 when it hosted the inaugural Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km venue that hosted the Middle East's inaugural Formula One race and continues to stage the annual Bahrain Grand Prix alongside various other motorsport events. The FIA Grade 1 licensed facility has accommodated GP2 racing, endurance competitions, and Australian V8 Supercars (2006-2010), while offering multiple track configurations for different racing series.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located near Barcelona in Catalonia, this 4. 657-kilometer motorsport facility features a balanced design combining extended straights with diverse corner configurations, making it well-suited for comprehensive vehicle performance evaluation. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstand structures.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Belgium's Spa-Francorchamps circuit, stretching over 7 kilometres through the Walloon countryside near Stavelot, has served as the home of the Belgian Grand Prix since the inaugural Formula One season in 1950. The venue has maintained an unbroken presence on the championship calendar from 1985 onwards, with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve spans 4. 361 kilometers and serves as the permanent home of Canada's Formula One Grand Prix. Beyond single-seaters, the track has accommodated various international motorsport series including sports car championships and North American racing categories.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading District, this Chinese motorsport facility hosted the Chinese Grand Prix annually between 2004 and 2019, then resumed the event from 2024 onward. The venue has expanded its motorsport calendar to include electric racing championships alongside its primary Formula One commitment.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Silverstone is an English racing venue located near Northamptonshire that has hosted the British Grand Prix since 1948 and notably staged the inaugural World Championship race in 1950. The circuit shared hosting duties for Britain's premier motorsport event with Aintree and Brands Hatch between 1955 and 1986 before becoming its permanent home from 1987 onwards.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, located near Budapest in Mogyoród, hosts the Hungarian Grand Prix on its 4. 381 km layout. Constructed in just eight months starting in late 1985, it became the first Formula One circuit to operate behind the Iron Curtain when it held its inaugural race in March 1986.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Milan in northern Italy, the Autodromo Nazionale Monza is a 5. 793 km track constructed in 1922 as mainland Europe's oldest purpose-built racing circuit. The venue has hosted the Italian Grand Prix continuously since 1949, except for a 1980 closure during renovation, earning its reputation as "the Temple of Speed" through its notably fast layout featuring extended straights and high-speed turns.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka International Racing Course, situated in Mie Prefecture, Japan, is a 5. 807 km circuit operated by Honda Mobilityland with a capacity of 155,000 spectators. The track serves as a premier venue for Formula One competition and has established itself as a significant racing destination for international motorsport.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that snakes through Paradise, Nevada, utilizing roads adjacent to the famous Las Vegas Strip along Las Vegas Boulevard. The track passes iconic landmarks including casinos and hotels such as Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, as well as the MSG Sphere venue.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the 4. 304 km Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez honors two Mexican racing brothers who died in separate accidents during the 1960s and early 1970s. The venue has hosted Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix intermittently since 2015, following earlier stints on different configurations, with the modern race now branded as the Mexico City Grand Prix.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens that hosts the Miami Grand Prix. Spanning 3. 363 miles with 19 corners, the track achieves qualifying speeds averaging 139 mph and was specifically designed by specialist circuit architects for its debut on the Formula One calendar in 2022.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street track that winds through Monte Carlo and La Condamine in the Principality of Monaco, circling the harbour area. Though officially named after the circuit itself, it is widely known as Monte Carlo since most of the layout traverses that particular neighbourhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the coastal dunes near Zandvoort in the Netherlands, this 4. 259 km track sits approximately 35 kilometers west of Amsterdam and hosted the Dutch Grand Prix when it rejoined the Formula One calendar in 2021. The circuit's partnership with Formula One will conclude following the 2026 season.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: Located north of Doha in Qatar, the Lusail International Circuit is a 5. 419-kilometre track featuring a 1. 068-kilometre main straight and holding FIA Grade 1 certification.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos, a 4. 309 km circuit in São Paulo, Brazil, opened in 1940 and was later renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace, who perished in an aviation accident eight years earlier. The track operates in a counterclockwise direction and features an associated karting facility dedicated to fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: A street circuit tracing the Jeddah Corniche waterfront along the Red Sea, this Saudi Arabian venue has hosted the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix annually since its 2021 debut. The track has also recently welcomed Formula E racing to its schedule from 2025 onwards.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's Marina Bay area, incorporating sections of the Downtown Core and Kallang districts into its street-based layout.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: The Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya, located near Barcelona in Catalonia, spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of extended straightaways and diverse corner types that test multiple racing skills. The facility holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas near Austin hosts the Formula One United States Grand Prix on its 5. 5-kilometer Grade 1 track, alongside NASCAR and motorcycle racing events. Beyond its current roster, the facility has previously accommodated various international racing series including IndyCar, endurance, and rallycross championships.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon, a Thai-British racing driver, currently races for Williams in Formula One under the Thai national flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he has secured two world championships with Renault in 2005 and 2006 while accumulating 32 Grand Prix victories throughout his 23-season career. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, winning the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, two Le Mans 24-hour races, and the Daytona 24 Hours, making him the sole driver to claim both Formula One and World Endurance world titles.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli joined Mercedes' Formula One lineup starting in 2025 and has already secured six race victories in his early career with the team.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British motorsport competitor who currently races in Formula One with the Haas team.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Gabi Bortoleto, a Brazilian motorsport competitor, currently races for Audi in the Formula One championship series.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from a 13-season career that includes 10 Grand Prix victories. He previously achieved runner-up finishes in the World Drivers' Championship during 2019 and 2020 while competing for Mercedes.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine motorsport competitor who currently races in Formula One for the Alpine team.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Australian driver Jack Doohan currently holds a reserve role with Haas in Formula One while actively competing in the LMP2 category of the European Le Mans Series with Nielsen Racing. He has made seven Grand Prix appearances spanning the 2024 and 2025 seasons.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The 2020 Italian Grand Prix victory with AlphaTauri represents a career highlight for the driver.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar is a French-Algerian motorsport competitor who races for Red Bull Racing in Formula One, representing France in the championship.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari, holding a record-equalling seven world championship titles alongside Michael Schumacher. The veteran competitor leads in numerous statistical categories, including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes throughout the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: Nicolas Hülkenberg, a German driver, currently races in Formula One for Audi. Beyond single-seater competition, he has achieved significant success in endurance motorsport, including a victory at the prestigious 24-hour race at Le Mans in 2015 while driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand racing driver currently competing in Formula One with Racing Bulls.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: The Monégasque driver currently races for Ferrari in Formula One, having claimed nine Grand Prix victories throughout his career spanning nine seasons. Leclerc finished as championship runner-up in 2022, marking his closest finish to the world title.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish driver currently competing in endurance racing for BMW and part-time in NASCAR, having previously participated in Formula One across two separate periods from 2014 to 2020 and again from 2022 to 2024.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris is a British Formula One driver for McLaren who claimed the 2025 drivers' championship. The 2025 season marked his eighth in the sport, during which he has accumulated 13 Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. Previously, he achieved a career highlight by winning the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while competing for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez competes in Formula One for Cadillac and has achieved six Grand Prix victories throughout his 15-year career in the sport. He finished as championship runner-up in 2023 while driving for Red Bull.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Australian driver Oscar Piastri currently races for McLaren in Formula One, having accumulated nine Grand Prix victories since joining the grid four seasons ago.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known by the nickname "the Honey Badger," competed in Formula One over a 14-year span from 2011 through 2024, claiming eight Grand Prix victories during his career in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, having secured seven Grand Prix victories throughout his eight-season career in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Carlos Sainz is a Spanish Formula One driver currently racing for Williams who has secured four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver who competed in Formula One during the 2023 and 2024 seasons. He currently races in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category for Proton Competition, following previous appearances in IMSA's LMP2 class.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently racing for Aston Martin, competing at the sport's highest level.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese driver, held reserve driver positions with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls throughout his Formula One career spanning 2021 to 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Dutch-Belgian driver Max Verstappen has claimed four consecutive world championships between 2021 and 2024 while racing for Red Bull Racing, accumulating 71 Grand Prix victories over his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu is a Chinese racing driver currently employed as a reserve driver for Cadillac in Formula One. He competed as a race driver in the championship between 2022 and 2024, establishing himself as the sole Chinese competitor to have participated in the sport.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: Alpine Racing operates as the Enstone-based Formula One outfit that succeeded Renault's works team following a 2021 rebranding intended to showcase the luxury sports car marque. The team achieved a single victory during its Alpine tenure when Esteban Ocon triumphed at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix, competing with Mercedes power units and holding a French racing licence until Renault's departure from the sport concluded at the end of 2025.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British automotive manufacturer, has entered Formula One racing through multiple organizational structures, with its current incarnation operating as AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker Ferrari, stands as Formula One's longest-running and most accomplished team, participating in every championship season since the sport's inaugural 1950 World Championship. Known colloquially as "the Prancing Horse" for their iconic emblem, the squad remains the oldest continuously competing outfit in the sport's history.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: American Formula One team established by NASCAR owner Gene Haas and competing since 2016, currently led by team principal Ayao Komatsu following Guenther Steiner's departure in early 2024.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: A Swiss engineering firm established in 1970, the outfit competed in Formula One from 1993 onwards as an independent constructor while building a legacy in endurance racing, including Le Mans victory in 1989. Following numerous organizational changes over three decades, the team departed the sport in 2025 as one of the championship's longest-serving constructors before being acquired by Audi to establish their works racing programme.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren is a British Formula One outfit headquartered in Woking that competes under corporate sponsorship. The team operates as part of the broader McLaren Group, which is owned by Bahrain's sovereign wealth fund.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a presence in Formula One since 1954 as both constructor and power unit supplier. The modern Mercedes-AMG Petronas team, based in Brackley and holding a German licence, became a three-way partnership in 2022 involving Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff in equal shares. The team carries the historic "Silver Arrows" designation associated with Mercedes' racing heritage.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that began competing in 2024 as one of two Red Bull-owned teams alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with operations in Milton Keynes, the squad operates as a sister team within the Red Bull GmbH motorsport division.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that commenced competition in 2024, operating as one of two Red Bull-owned squads alongside Red Bull Racing. Headquartered in Faenza with operations in Milton Keynes, the team functions as part of the Austrian conglomerate's dual-team Formula One structure.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing is an Austrian-licensed Formula One team headquartered in England and owned by Red Bull GmbH since its 2005 establishment. Led by Christian Horner until 2025, the team was succeeded in management by Laurent Mekies as part of Red Bull's portfolio that also includes the Racing Bulls team.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering, established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head following the collapse of Williams's earlier F1 venture, represents one of Formula One's storied British constructors. Headquartered at a substantial facility in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team competes in the championship under the Atlassian Williams F1 Team designation from 2026 onwards.
